record.paper_title: Open Problems in Applying Random-Matrix Theory to Nuclear Reactions
record.original_question: Do shell-model configurations and compound-nucleus resonances at excitation energies lying midway between two major nuclear shells exhibit the mixing and spectral-fluctuation behavior expected from the GOE, or does the GOE expectation established within a single major shell fail or change in that between-shell regime?

evidence.quote: To be sure, the mixing addressed in Ref. [13] refers only to the configurations within a single major shell. Shell structure being manifest over a wide range of excitation energies, one may wonder what happens at excitation energies that lie in the middle between two major shells. That question seems not to have been addressed in the theoretical literature.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the nuclear shell model, single-particle orbitals are grouped into "major shells" separated by relatively large energy gaps. For a fixed number of valence nucleons distributed within a single major shell, it is known that the residual two-body interaction induces strong configuration mixing, and that the resulting many-body energy spectrum exhibits spectral-fluctuation properties (e.g., nearest-neighbor level-spacing distribution, Dyson–Mehta Δ₃ statistic) consistent with the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) of random-matrix theory: a probability measure on the space of real symmetric N×N matrices H with density proportional to exp(−(N/4λ²) tr H²) that is invariant under orthogonal conjugation.

Now consider the regime in which the excitation energy lies midway between two adjacent major shells, so that the relevant Hilbert space is built from many-body configurations involving particle-hole excitations spanning two (or more) different major shells, mixed by the residual interaction.

Question: Determine whether, in this between-shells regime, the configuration mixing and the spectral fluctuations of the resulting many-body Hamiltonian (and of compound-nucleus resonances at the corresponding excitation energies) still conform to GOE predictions, or whether systematic deviations from GOE statistics arise as a consequence of the inter-shell structure. Provide either (i) a theoretical demonstration that GOE behavior persists across the between-shells regime, or (ii) an identification and characterization of the deviations from GOE behavior occurring there.
artifact.category_tag: Random-matrix theory in nuclear shell model
artifact.status_search_result: Searches return general studies of GOE-type spectral fluctuations within single major shells (e.g., sd-shell, A=32, Xe-136) and some indications of deviations from GOE in rare-earth nuclei attributed to configuration/deformation effects, but no direct theoretical treatment of the mixing and spectral statistics specifically at excitation energies midway between two major shells. The question therefore appears to remain unaddressed in the theoretical literature, with status undetermined.

status_evidence.title: Spectral statistics of rare-earth nuclei: Investigation of shell model configuration effect
status_evidence.snippet: An obvious deviation from GOE is observed for considered nuclei and there are some suggestions about the effect due to mass, deformation parameter and shell model configurations.
status_evidence.claim: Shell-model configurations affect GOE conformance, but the analysis is within standard shell-model spaces, not between-shell regimes.

status_evidence.title: Spectral fluctuations in Xe-136 using the shell model
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral fluctuations of full shell-model Hamiltonians are well characterized by the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble.
status_evidence.claim: GOE-like behavior is established for shell-model spaces within a single major shell.

status_evidence.title: Spectral Fluctuations in A=32 Nuclei Using the Framework of the Nuclear Shell Model
status_evidence.snippet: Statistics correspond to GOE predictions for sd-shell calculations.
status_evidence.claim: Existing GOE confirmations are within a single major shell, leaving the inter-shell regime unaddressed.
